branches.reason: Someone could use the exposed payment details to make unauthorised transactions.

steps.title: Contact your bank
steps.instructions: Use the number on your card or in your banking app. Ask about replacing the card, check recent transactions and turn on transaction alerts.

branches.reason: These details could help someone impersonate you or open credit in your name.

steps.title: Check for unfamiliar credit activity
steps.instructions: Review your credit report where available. If you see an account or application you do not recognise, contact the organisation directly using its official details.

branches.reason: Someone could try the exposed password on this service or anywhere you reused it.

steps.title: Change the password for this service
steps.instructions: Open the service directly and use its security settings to set a new, unique password. If you cannot sign in, use the service’s official password reset.

steps.title: Replace reused passwords
steps.instructions: If you used this password on other accounts, change each one to a different password. Start with your email and financial accounts.

steps.title: Add a second sign-in step
steps.instructions: Turn on a passkey or two-factor authentication where available, then sign out any sessions you do not recognise.

branches.reason: Exposed answers can help someone get through account recovery.

steps.title: Replace exposed recovery answers
steps.instructions: Change your security answers on the breached service and any other account where you reused them.

branches.reason: Someone could use an exposed address to make a call or message sound legitimate.

steps.title: Check unexpected messages about your address
steps.instructions: If a message mentions a delivery or your home address, check it through the sender’s official website or app before replying or paying.

branches.reason: Your number could be used in targeted calls or attempts to take control of your SIM.

steps.title: Protect your phone number
steps.instructions: Ask your carrier if it offers a SIM-swap or port-out PIN. Where available, use a passkey or authenticator app for important accounts.

branches.reason: Someone could use these details to make an email about this service look genuine.

steps.title: Check unexpected messages about this service
steps.instructions: Open the service directly instead of following a link in an unexpected message. Look up any warning in your account.

stealer.reason: Malware can steal saved sign-ins and keep collecting new ones from the same device.

steps.title: Check the affected device for malware
steps.instructions: Run a full scan with trusted security software. Use a different device you trust for sensitive sign-ins while you investigate.

steps.title: Secure your accounts from a trusted device
steps.instructions: Change the passwords for email, banking and your password manager first. Sign out other sessions and check recovery addresses and forwarding rules.

fallback.reason: Exposed account details can make impersonation messages sound more convincing.

steps.title: Review the account’s security settings
steps.instructions: Open the service directly, review recent sign-ins and check whether two-factor authentication is available.
